entries.note: Reader must structurally detect dataModelRevision generation and refuse to coerce/skip unsupported ones — migration over drift, corpus-wide.
Display label/hint explicitly barred from carrying semantic weight (validation, Relations, Discovery) — identifier over label.
A Type can't reuse a Field's identity for different semantics; new meaning requires a new Field id, not overloading the existing one.
Semantic content (aiGuidance) belongs to the Field's own identity; Type-level framing doesn't redefine it.
Pure internal referential-integrity rule for a Type's own lifecycle definition; no clear axis tradeoff.
Same as initialState rule — internal well-formedness of lifecycle.transitions[], not a grid-axis preference.
Record.lifecycleState must declared-reference a key in the Type's own states — cross-entity declared linkage, but weak fit.
Every fieldId used in a Package's Types must be catalogued in dependencyRefs — catalog over circumstance.
Bundled mode requires the catalog (dependencyRefs) to be backed by actual Field entries — catalog completeness, not assumed availability.
Field.id is stable; a new id (not an edit) is what makes something a new definition — identifier over label, textbook fit.
Cross-field rules can only reference fields within the Type's own effective field list — declared scope over reaching outside.
Pure shape/parameter requirements per validation-rule type; no evident grid tradeoff.
View compatibility is field-centric, not Type-bound — favors field-level identity over the coarser Type label/grouping.
FieldView rendering hints (displayLabel/displayHint/compositeRenderer/editorHintOverride) barred from affecting semantics — identifier over label.
A View must not redefine the semantic content of a Field or Type it references — semantic ownership stays with the Field's identity.
typeId used by a View must be catalogued in dependencyRefs (and present in types[] when bundled) — catalog over circumstance.
Fixes which Relation endpoint is the asserting instance and forbids reversing it — statement over side-effect.
Reserves Relation for real semantic-consequence assertions and bars using it for lightweight prose mention — declared strength over convenient reach.
NoteSection.name must be unique within a Note — the name functions as a local identifier.
TypedField.name must be unique within a TypedRecord — same local-identifier pattern as NoteSection.name.
Container.containerId is explicitly not an instance ID and can't appear as a Relation endpoint — declared containment boundary, not location/reach.
Container root/member lists must reference valid instance IDs — containment membership must be a real declared reference.
typeId/typeVersion are authoritative over the denormalised typeNamespace/typeName convenience labels — identifier over label, direct fit.
ProtocolStage.dependsOn must reference a stageId declared within the enclosing Protocol — declared scope over reaching outside it.
ProtocolStage.contributesTo must resolve within the stage's own or the Protocol's declared effective field list — same declared-scope pattern as dependsOn.
dependsOn is the declared-reference authority for execution order; the order field is a convenient positional default that must not contradict it.
explicitly frames namespace/name form as required for cross-package resolution; bare strings leave portability of the section undefined.
containerId must resolve to a valid Container reference; other Address fields stay optional pending focus narrowing.
renderViewId must resolve to a declared View.id, with a stricter physical-presence requirement in bundled mode.
TypeRef.typeId across several Blueprint fields must resolve via dependencyRefs, with bundled mode requiring physical presence.
Protocol/type and field references must resolve via dependencyRefs, with bundled mode requiring physical presence.
sets one canonical interpretation (ignore format when datatype isn't string) that all implementations must follow uniformly.
extendsTypeId must resolve to a valid Type; the acyclicity clause is a secondary structural touch.
a field-duplication-across-inheritance rule; doesn't map cleanly onto any cell's stated preference.
fieldOrder completeness/no-duplicate-no-omission rule is a narrow structural detail without a clean cell match.
override fieldId must resolve to an inherited field; the Field-semantics-immutability clause is a secondary touch.
the full transitive closure of base Types must be explicitly declared in dependencyRefs, not left to convenient reach.
NavigationLink endpoints must resolve to a sectionId declared in the enclosing DocumentView.
defines the structural markers (.srs marker + manifest.json) that make a directory a conforming repository.
the tree-enumerated instance set is the authoritative catalog; there is no manifest index to cross-check against (RFC-038 R1/R2).
the manifest's declared embedded Container takes precedence over a separately-located container.json on conflict.
a repository-document SourceReference must resolve to a present sidecar; an unresolved documentId is invalid.
archive completeness is measured against the tree-enumerated catalog, not the retired manifest instanceIndex (RFC-038 R1/R2).
bundled local-package completeness is measured against the tree-enumerated instance set (RFC-038 R1), not a manifest index.
archives must preserve referenced source-document material outright rather than relying on it being recognized/resolved elsewhere.
a sidecar's contentPath must resolve to an existing file; an unresolved reference is invalid and must be surfaced before use.
repositoryId, not incidental circumstance, must be the identifier an importer keys existing-repo detection off of.
a conflict must be surfaced as an explicit statement rather than resolved via a silent overwrite/discard side effect.
establishes one canonical checksum string format across every checksum-bearing field in the corpus.
ExactTypeRef entries must resolve within the in-scope Package union; unresolved entries are diagnosed and excluded from matching.
Resolved root Type is authoritative over the declared containerType label (mismatch only diagnostic, never invalidates).
Vocabulary Terms give tags one canonical resolution over free-string synonyms, but only when a Vocabulary governs the key.
A mandatory operation providing an authoritative, always-consistent catalog of container membership across the repo.
ExactTypeRef (typeId+version) requires fully declared, resolved references rather than loose/convenient ones.
Root Container is explicitly declared in manifest.container rather than inferred from tree location.
Root container membership resolves against the tree-enumerated authoritative set, not a retired manifest instanceIndex.
identityInstanceId is the repository's identity pointer; atomic reassignment guarantees it never names a non-member.
Navigation sections should be backed by a declared Container in the container set, not merely implied by structure.
typeId/fieldId references must resolve across the full multi-version package union; also touches portability (must not remove a version directory a reference still needs).
upstreamPackage.packageId must be backed by an explicit matching packageRefs entry, not assumed.
core types/fields are resolvable the same single way in every repository without per-repo packageRef configuration.
Reserving com.semanticops.core against local/external redeclaration enforces one unambiguous namespace owner.
Adds a type constraint on the repository's identity record; migration-period warning-vs-error behavior is a secondary governance touch.
Disjointness between sourceRole enum and RelationTypeDefinition keys prevents two systems giving one key ambiguous meaning.
Extension declaration strictly bounds which implementations the cross-field-validation rules apply to.
Mandates one prescribed evaluation model (fail-all, not fail-first) for implementations that opt in.
Narrow firing semantics of one rule type; doesn't map to a governing-preference axis.
Domain-specific field-ordering comparison semantics, not a structural design axis.
Narrow mutual-exclusion counting rule; no clear fit among the twelve cells.
Field-eligibility constraints for one rule type are extension-internal detail, not a Pattern Grid concern.
Unknown rule types must be rejected rather than silently tolerated, keeping the extension's rule set closed to one set of behaviors.
Cross-type property leakage between rule shapes is schema-purity detail, too narrow to anchor to one cell.
validationRules must be explicitly restated by a subtype rather than inherited as a side effect of extension.
A lifecycle state's relation obligation must be satisfied by an actual asserted Relation, not treated as incidental.
newRecord fulfillment creates an explicit successor Record atomically rather than overwriting, with the relation asserted alongside it.

Core mechanic is resolving a viewId reference to a DocumentView, with ambiguous/unresolved references erroring out — declared strength over convenient reach; also touches conformance for the fallback-selection algorithm.
Prescribes exact must-include/must-not-include query semantics for structured filters, i.e. one correct result set over many possible interpretations.
Explicitly mandates uniform wrapping behavior across every datatype rather than per-type special-casing.

Routes successor-flow presentation 'from structure rather than state-name matching' — declared structural reference over convenient string matching; secondary touch to succession via state transitions.
Governs how a type-query's container scope is determined (explicit/repository/subtree) via declared containerScope and contains-relation traversal.

Explicit declared memberOrder takes precedence over the default topological-sort fallback, echoing declared-strength-over-convenient-reach; could also read as containment given container-subset framing.
Byte-for-byte reproducible archive export excluding host-specific metadata is exactly preserve-over-recognize.
fieldMeta's {source, editedAt, sourceRefs} shape is explicit stated provenance on a field value; the surrounding rule is a structural key-subset validation.
Attachment must be an explicit SourceReference statement and MUST NOT be modeled as a Relation edge — statement over side-effect, verbatim.
Defines a single deterministic order of inclusion-then-exclusion filtering and required no-op behavior when the field or extension is absent.
Keys projected fields by Field.name and retires the ProjectedFieldGroup/ProjectedGroupEntry constructs entirely — one name over many, directly.
Declared structured-filter constraints cannot be widened or overridden by convenient content-match recall — declared strength over convenient reach, verbatim shape.
Protects a live pinned typeId+typeVersion reference from deletion so the Record-to-Field edge doesn't break; also touches governance (type version lifecycle).
Forbids path traversal reaching outside the declared co-located directory — convenient reach disallowed in favor of the strict declared relationship.
Mandates uniform graceful load behavior when an optional package/record is absent, rather than implementation-variable refusal.
precedes MUST be interpreted as a semantic claim, not a rendering hint — statement over side-effect, verbatim.
Bounds diagnostic/enforcement behavior for policy thresholds but explicitly permits implementation choice (MAY enforce hard rejection), weakening the one-way fit.
Clarifies the scope of the recall-floor guarantee — inclusion is fixed, rank order is explicitly left free.
Mandates AND semantics for multi-value tag predicates (one interpretation over the ambiguous alternative); the Vocabulary canonicalization clause leans toward description as a secondary touch.
Requires one canonical key-serialization order (by FieldAssignment.order) so re-runs are byte-idempotent, rather than allowing varying orders.
contentPath resolution is anchored strictly relative to the declared sourceDocumentsPath base.
A tombstoned reference (documentId) remains valid and conformant even when the convenient reach (actual content bytes) is unavailable.
Defines the mandatory text-projection segments but explicitly allows implementations to differ on optional displayLabel segments, weakening a clean one-way fit.
Duplicate Field.name within a Type's effective field set is rejected as fatal at definition time, not resolved by precedence — matches Earth's 'identity conflicts are fatal' column principle.
Precisely enumerates which datatype/format combinations MUST or MUST NOT contribute text-projection segments — one determinate searchability rule over variance.
Fixes one normative algorithm for combining typeFilter and memberOrder that all implementations must follow, over any local variant.
Mandates a single required recall-floor matching algorithm for ext:discovery implementations.
Fixes one canonical normalization algorithm (NFC + case fold) all implementations must use for matching, over ad-hoc variants.
Key absence is ruled the sole representation of unset, forbidding null as an alternate representation -- one shape over many.
A scoping clarification (schema covers fieldValues, not envelope members) rather than an instance of any single cell's over-preference.
Field.name verbatim is the one required key form at every depth, with no case/separator transform -- one name over many.
Prescribes one uniform default behavior for absent policy that all implementations must apply.
Deterministic archive production rules fix one exact byte-level output over many possible valid ZIPs.
sourceId must resolve via the declared sidecar mechanism, not the convenient content file -- declared strength over convenient reach.
Clarifies conformance surface: extra results beyond the mandated recall floor don't violate the one required behavior.
Singleton-per-repository constraint on the policy record with duplicate handling, tying uniqueness to the repository catalog.
Defines a fixture-driven conformance test implementations MUST pass exactly -- explicit one-way-over-many machinery.
Defines a fixture-driven conformance test (superset requirement) implementations MUST pass.
Version-gated removal of deprecated field-group machinery with explicit revision resolution -- migration over drift.
Fixes one exact filtering algorithm (OR semantics, absent-state exclusion) all implementations of the query must follow.
Requires fieldValues keys to equal Field.name from the effective field set, rejecting unknowns -- one naming scheme over many.
A reference value must resolve to an instance matching the declared rangeType, not merely a reachable target -- declared strength over convenient reach.
Requires identifying file type by content magic bytes, not filename or MIME label -- identifier over label.

Defines the canonical three-condition container membership test (declared root/member lists plus transitive contains), though it also touches repository via the tree-authoritative-over-manifest-cache point.
Removes current defaultValue sites now and defers a single future layered-override capability, explicitly ruling out a second parallel mechanism -- migration over drift.
Explicitly rules the Attribution cell's foundation principle (stated over assumed, testimony never authority).
Explicitly labeled Cell: Conformance -- a single registry replacing hand-wired checks.
Meta-guidance on what belongs in the decision log itself, not a data-model preference instance of any of the twelve cells.
Explicitly labeled Cell: Versioning -- semantic content changes by increment/successor, with state fields carved out as the sanctioned in-place exception.
Unknown instance-layer content must be preserved (or loudly refused), never silently discarded -- preserve over recognize.
Records are the single semantic source with docs/schema generated from them — one canonical description, many derived renderings.
States what counts as the repository's authoritative catalog versus manifest.json — a repository/catalog-authority claim.
A view-vs-type layering rule (expression never alters meaning) rather than a Pattern Grid preference claim.
Self-declared Cell: Conformance — collapses parallel workflow-state mechanisms into one Lifecycle way.
Systemic evidence-driven removal of dormant constructs from the standard; individual removed items carry their own separate cell tags.
Self-declared Cell: Identity — collapses the tier model, identifier-bearing Record vs free-text Note.
One target-neutral intermediate representation ahead of any backend — one way over many render paths.
Charter-level rule for axis 5-11 (Succession↔Conformance); the three layer mechanisms are unified under the Fire-column successor-over-overwrite preference (record's own tag: cell:succession).
Explicitly invokes Description's preference: a name is a contract, renamed only via migration, never a lingering alias.
Keeps rendering hints out of fieldType facets — a presentation/meaning layer-boundary rule, not a cell preference.
One declared release governs rendering behavior — one way over many, changed only via reviewable commit.
Unifies the substrate escape-bag name to 'meta' everywhere — one name over many, executed as a migration.
Explicitly a KEYED-reference design (cites rfc-decision-c8704763) for SectionSource's typeKey resolution.
Meaning must live once in the records, not split off into a hand-maintained overlay — one canonical description.
Self-declared Cell: Governance — sets the decision-mode machinery (clear/complicated/complex/chaotic).
Field identity within a Record recovered via name plus pinned Type rather than a repeated fieldId; also touches the Reference cell's PINNED strength.
Composes two migrations into one release train at a declared dataModelRevision — migration over drift.
States the axis 6-12 travel mandate directly: every held construct must have a travelling form.
Self-declared Cell: Governance — adds reach-marking, sequence-propagation, and balance-count operations to the framework.
Renames DocumentView to Composition and retires 'Export' as vocabulary — one name over many.
Explicitly framed as a companion register to the Pattern Grid governing layer-stacking, not a cell placement itself.
Self-declared Cell: Governance — adds autoclassification and the stance vocabulary as grid operations.
Field structure decomposed into independent fieldType facets; a type-system design choice not clearly tied to one of the twelve preferences.
Self-declared Cell: Reference — defines the four reference strengths (PINNED/LINEAGE/KEYED/LOCATOR).
The founding ratification of the Pattern Grid itself (all axes and cell preferences at once), not a placement into one cell.

Describes migrating the metamodel from RFC-004's parallel schema-source vocabulary into the canonical self-hosted package — a systemic migration-over-drift move, though it also touches conformance's single-source theme.
Authoritative-vs-approximated classification exists precisely to ensure emitters preserve information rather than silently dropping it — preserve over recognize.
States directly that reference-mode is a declared, weaker link (target id) that must not be conflated with a Relation — the reference cell's own distinction.
Turns on whether changing the value set requires a new Field version (allowedValues) or not (vocabularyRef) — the increment-over-edit tradeoff.
Normalizes absent status to a single interpretation across all resolution rules, i.e. one consistent reading rather than many.
A field-requiredness inheritance rule for specializing the substrate Type — doesn't cleanly match any single cell's preference; leaning none over forcing containment or succession.
Defines exactly what a 'conforming implementation' must be able to compute — the canonical one-way-over-many requirement.

Exclusivity between allowedValues and a vocabularyRef, plus the requirement that the ref resolve to a closed Vocabulary, is about the declared strength of that field-to-vocabulary reference; conformance is a plausible secondary read.
Governs reusing a retired key without silently overwriting stale references — successor over overwrite, with a reference-integrity secondary touch.
When two statuses could both apply, mandates one canonical status to report — one way over many.
Defines the `.srs` marker as what makes a directory a repository, independent of where it sits — catalog over circumstance, the repository cell's core claim.
Mandates one consistent fallback behavior (ignore, don't error) for implementations lacking the extension.
Uniqueness requirement on asset names within a Theme — identifier discipline over label collision.
A bundled ThemeReference's themeId must actually resolve within Package.themes[] — declared reference must hold, not just be conveniently reachable.
Requires implementations to emit the same semantic CSS classes for html/pdf output — one prescribed rendering behavior.
Mandates a single uniform fallback (empty string) for inapplicable template variables across all implementations.
A definitional table fixing one canonical meaning per template variable name — one name over many possible readings.
Same ignore-don't-error mandate as r1, restated as a numbered rule [T-1] — one required behavior.
A minimum-cardinality validation rule on Theme.targets; doesn't clearly map to a single cell's preference, so leaning none.
Prescribes exactly one behavior (apply vs ignore the Theme) keyed on format membership in targets.
Forbids the presentation layer from suppressing or reordering structural content passed through {{content}} — preserving structure over letting theming recognize/alter it.
Restates the asset-name uniqueness constraint as rule [T-4] — identifier uniqueness within the Theme.
Restates the bundled-theme resolution requirement as [T-5] — a declared reference that must actually resolve.
Requires one uniform pass-through behavior for unrecognized template variables rather than implementation-specific errors.
Forbids re-emitting structural headings outside {{content}} in wrapper templates — preserving the one structural rendering over letting theme templates re-derive it.
Fixes the one correct override-precedence and no-duplicate-key behavior for wrapper templates.
Mandates uniform CSS-class application and normalization; subsidiary clause echoes identity's Field.name-over-displayLabel preference.
Specifies the one correct fieldRow application order/filter and a non-wrap constraint on preamble.
Requires uniform acceptance of a new definitionType value without validation error.
Dispatch-precedence rule: exactly one of two template mechanisms applies depending on compositeRenderer.
Defines the single correct silent-ignore behavior for unmatched keys.
Precedence rule between groupFieldRowTemplates and fieldRow, one way to resolve the conflict.
Fixes the default CSS class value implementations must use absent explicit config.
Specifies exact output behavior for an explicit empty-string override.
Scopes template application strictly to the matching renderer, excluding others.
Names the single authoritative signal for format-conditional default resolution.
Silent-ignore rule for unknown config properties, one uniform behavior.
Consolidated processing rules for compositeRendererConfig keying, format signal, and sentinel handling.
States defaults are output specification applied unconditionally, not optional configuration.
Defines exact applicability conditions for compositeFieldRowTemplates versus renderer dispatch.
Deprecation/migration rule requiring keys be carried forward at the #242 cutover rather than silently lost.
Ties rule retirement to the FieldGroup removal cutover, a deliberate migration timeline rather than drift.
Core claim is deriving the identity class from the stable Field.name rather than the human-facing displayLabel.
Broadens a rendering requirement to apply unconditionally regardless of extension declaration.
Explicit dual-emission deprecation window tied to a named cutover clock, then retirement of the old form.
Fixes the fallback behavior at the terminal rung of the row-template resolution ladder.
Requires a fresh, distinct UUID for the archive rather than reusing/implying the origin's identity; also touches portability's standalone-artifact concern.
Defines the closure of instances, definitions, relations, and content that MUST be preserved when exporting a slice across the repository boundary.
Cross-boundary relations are preserved as externalRelationRefs provenance rather than requiring in-archive recognition/resolution.
Relaxes validator recognition requirements for a partial/boundary-crossing slice while real integrity errors still count.
initialState must reference the state's key by declared identifier rather than convenient positional reach; the co-occurring uniqueness constraint (exactly one isInitial) is a secondary touch.
A validity constraint tying a state's isInitial flag to its status; no grid axis (identity/versioning/description/attribution etc.) is the primary claim here.
Constrains which transitions (state-to-state sequencing) are valid, forbidding a final state from being a transition source.
Declared identityFieldId is preferred as the one canonical display label over any implementation-specific heuristic — one name over many.
identityFieldId must resolve to an actual fieldId in the Type's effective field set — a declared reference that must resolve, not a convenient/loose pointer.

Governs which single field supplies a section's heading label (identityFieldId as fallback, titleFieldId taking precedence when declared) — a display-label resolution rule; also touches the multi-site precedence pattern seen in reference/conformance rules.
Fixes one canonical syntactic form for renderer identifiers, with graceful degradation for anything else — one way over many, enforced at render/validation time.
Explicitly labeled Governance in the text: bare renderer names are namespace-controlled and only enter via ratified RFC, vs. vendor-namespaced free introduction — controlled evolution over drift.
A binding must reference a Field of the correct declared type/mode (ref, inline) to be honored; otherwise it is not treated as a valid reference.
A binding's fieldId must actually resolve on the rendered instance's Type to take effect; otherwise it is silently inert — reference validity scoped to what's actually assigned.
Binding must target a field directly assigned to the Type; no inference is permitted for nested composites — declared strength over convenient/implicit reach.

A deterministic multi-site precedence algorithm resolves at most one binding among several possible declaration sites — one way over many possible orderings; also touches reference (more-specific declared binding wins).
Standardized fallback behavior for an unrecognised renderer value, with mandatory diagnostic — one canonical degrade path over silently varying behavior.
A deterministic tie-break algorithm (lowest order, then code-point) picks exactly one winner among ambiguous role candidates — one way over many possible resolutions.
Defines a single standardized contract-satisfaction test a role Field must pass, with specified fallback on failure — process correctness, one way over many.
editorHintOverride, when a valid value, supersedes Field.editorHint for that View; an invalid value is dropped and the original applies — successor over overwrite, with a validity gate.
Standardizes diagnostic shape, identification, and severity across all CR-036-n rules, and pins that none affect exit code — one uniform diagnostic regime over many ad hoc ones.
Fixes the one baseline rendering path to use when no L1 View is selected, excluding L1 influence — one defined path over many possible fallbacks.
Normative, format-independent rules for which fields emit a row and how (no empty labels, block-list for multi-entry) — standardized rendering correctness.
Introduces the normative field-row emission forms as the terminal rung of a defined template ladder — largely framing text pointing at a standardized output contract.

Pins exact separator characters, element names/nesting/classes as normative per format, emitted unconditionally regardless of whether ext:themes-l1 is declared — one canonical baseline output over many.
Fixes multi-entry values to a single normative rendering form (block list, never comma-joined) across implementations.
Mandates a specific blank-line separation rule between rows, explicitly structural (CommonMark-driven) rather than cosmetic — one correct serialization over many.
Specifies exact per-format continuation-line indentation rules for multi-line values — standardized output form, one way per format.
Defines the one normative empty/placeholder emission behavior for the baseline path, distinct from the L1 path's own governing option — standardized process correctness.
Mandates one deterministic escaping/emission behavior per output format across all implementations, not per-instance naming.
Normatively fixes a single required resolution for {{heading-3}} in standalone context, forbidding the literal token — one way over many.
Fallback rule for choosing which field's value serves as a record's rendered heading/label when no title is declared; secondary touch on identity via identityFieldId.
Same pattern as r10: fixes JSON-mode heading-variable resolution to one required value, disallowing the literal token.
